findings.title: Package resolution may require setup and network access
findings.detail: The launch uses a package runner, which can resolve or install code depending on its cache and options. Server-internal installs are not determined by this scan.
findings.next_step: Check the runner's cache, package source, exact version, and documented setup/egress requirements in the target environment.

findings.title: An exact package pin was not confirmed
findings.detail: The limited direct-runner syntax check did not recognize an exact version. This is not proof that the package is unpinned.
findings.next_step: Review the launch syntax and lock/install procedure against the runner's documentation.

findings.title: Log mentions a missing runtime
findings.detail: The supplied text contains a missing-executable signal. It may describe a nested subprocess rather than the main server.
findings.next_step: Check which stage requested the executable and verify that stage's runtime requirements on the intended host.

findings.title: A timeout does not locate the failing stage
findings.detail: The supplied text mentions a timeout; it does not establish whether transport, HTTP, parsing, installation, or a subprocess stalled.
findings.next_step: Collect a minimized timeline for startup, network request, parsing/subprocess, and tool response before changing the timeout.

findings.title: Installer and protocol-error signals occur together
findings.detail: The supplied text contains both installer messages and protocol/JSON errors. This is a hypothesis: combined stdout/stderr logs do not prove stream contamination.
findings.next_step: Verify which stream carried installer output and whether dependency installation occurred during startup or the tool call.

findings.title: Registry and network-denial signals occur together
findings.detail: A package-registry reference and a denial signal appear in supplied text. Their causal relationship and current reachability are not verified.
findings.next_step: Check whether documented setup or a nested tool step needs registry access; confirm the existing policy with its owner.

limits: This is static triage of supplied files, not a connection or security test.
No server, command, package, or MCP tool is executed; no network is used.
Rules can miss problems and can match unrelated messages in combined logs.
No matched rule means not verified, not readiness or safety.
Local runtime checks, when requested, inspect this host's PATH only; configured paths and environments are not tested.
Reports omit raw names, arguments, environment values, endpoints, paths, and log excerpts. The original inputs remain local.
exit_zero_means: Analysis completed; it is not a readiness, safety, or connection result.
